reasoning:
**Question.** The last water level USGS reports on 31 December 2026 for gauge 10010000, Great Salt Lake at Saltair (the south arm), in feet to the nearest 0.1.

**Starting point.** The south arm stood at 4,190.3 ft on 22-23 Nov (HydroMap, citing USGS 10010000). TownLift (24 Nov) gives 4,190.2 ft as of 23 Nov, and the state's lake-elevation page 4,190.2 ft on 18 Nov. It is up about 0.2 ft in a week and 0.4 ft in 30 days, from roughly 4,189.7 ft in early October. Two lake-level aggregators show about 4,189.9 ft, but their numbers match the north arm gauge, not Saltair.

**Base rate.** The lake rises from late November: evaporation is almost nil and the rivers keep flowing. South arm, per KSL: 4,192.1 ft on 20 Nov 2024 to about 4,192.5 on 2 Jan 2025; 4,191.3 on 20 Nov 2025 to 4,191.6 in early Jan 2026 (Salt Lake Tribune). That is +0.25 to +0.4 ft by year-end; 2021 was nearer +0.15 and 2022 about +0.45, both approximate.

**This year.** The recent pace is faster than in those years, helped by a series of storms and probably by the causeway berm: the state said in August it would close it once the south arm fell to 4,190 ft, which keeps river inflow in the south arm (closure not confirmed). Against that, 2025-26 was a record-dry winter, so base flows are low, and the NWS forecast for Salt Lake City (24 Nov) is dry until rain chances return on 27-30 Nov. I take a gain of about +0.35 ft, range +0.1 to +0.7.

**Noise.** The resolving value is one reading at a gauge on the south shore, where wind can move the level a few tenths of a foot for hours. That widens both tails.

**Other outcomes.** At or below 4,190.4 needs a dry December or a southerly wind set-down at reading time (13%). At or above 4,190.9 needs a very wet December or a post-frontal surge (14%).

**Forecast.** Median 4,190.6 ft, with 62% on 4,190.5 to 4,190.7 and a 90% range of 4,190.3 to 4,191.0 ft.
question_title: What will be the water level of the Great Salt Lake on December 31, 2026?
